Key Research Thinking Patterns: Bias-Corrected Statistical Learning: Addresses sampling bias and demographic imbalance in predictive modeling by integrating Kernel Means Matching (KMM) with bi-level optimization frameworks to ensure equitable representation in user demographic prediction tasks.

Spectral Acceleration via Randomized Linear Algebra: Enhances the computational scalability of kernel methods and spectral estimation by employing Data-Dependent Random Projection (D2RP) and Random Feature-Based Power Iteration (RFPI), leveraging theoretical bounds from Random Matrix Theory.

Prototype-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization: Resolves dual imbalances (modality and class) in multimodal learning by implementing Prototype-Based Fully Balanced Learning (PFBL) and Prototype-Oriented Discriminative Enhancement (PODE) loss, utilizing constrained gradient optimization to stabilize cross-transformer fusion.

Disagreement-Based Active Learning: Optimizes data labeling efficiency and model fairness by deploying Disagreement-based Active Learning and Fairness-Aware Active Learning (D-FA2L) strategies, which iteratively select samples to minimize disparate impact while maximizing predictive accuracy.
Summary Description: Chao Lan specializes in algorithmic fairness, computational efficiency, and multimodal learning, focusing on robust, scalable solutions for social media analysis. Lan’s work addresses critical challenges in demographic bias mitigation and misinformation detection through advanced statistical and optimization techniques. Key contributions include Kernel Means Matching for bias correction, Data-Dependent Random Projection for high-dimensional acceleration, and Prototype-Based Fully Balanced Learning for multimodal fake news detection. By leveraging datasets like Twitter and Fakeddit, Lan develops methods that balance ethical considerations with computational performance, utilizing constrained gradient optimization and cross-transformer fusion to enhance model reliability across diverse data modalities.
